classes.name: Spiritmaster
classes.intro: Maintain spirits, deliberate summon setup and target debuffs. This baseline uses uncharged Fusion; charged variants require a different manual layout.
core: Basic attack support and spirit cycle.
opener: Build the relevant basic-attack setup.
Apply Flame Blessing and Spirit’s Benediction before Ancient Spirit.
Summon Ancient Spirit, then use available Fusion and Jointstrike windows.
Continue the two lines with Cold Shock; maintain debuffs without wasting resets.
progression: If Fusion has the charge specialty selected, remove it from this repeating setup and use it manually.
Do not assume a sixth-stigma regional guide fits Global’s four-slot baseline.
Destructive Attack is a deliberate loadout swap, not an additional fifth slot.
classes.gear: Prioritize core spell/spirit levels and sustainable offensive stats. Keep enough mana to sustain Cold Shock and the spirit cycle through movement-heavy fights.
classes.variant: Charged Fusion trades a different cast commitment against more frequent uncharged casts. Treat it as an alternative to test, not a universally superior upgrade.
classes.lab: Corrode uses a 20s base effect and 45s base cooldown in the Lab. The 30s duration requires its extension specialty. Summon/buff state and cooldown-reset specialties remain evidence-gated.
classes.pitfall: Do not refresh Corrode just because 20s passed if its actual cooldown is not ready; do not interrupt a charged skill with the macro.

classes.name: Cleric
classes.intro: Build a usable damage loop, but keep healing, protection and charge decisions manual. Group survival takes precedence over a dummy rotation.
core: Main damage investments as the build develops.
Keep the group alive before adding optional damage.
opener: Prepare the required protection toggle and safe positioning.
Apply your target setup deliberately.
Use Earth Punishment and the available damage line while the party is stable.
Interrupt the damage loop immediately for healing, cleanse or mechanics.
progression: Do not assume reset-dependent Condemnation behavior before its required specialty.
The damage preset is not a complete raid-healing prescription.
Level healing and recovery for the encounters you actually heal.
classes.gear: Balance core skill levels with mana sustainability and healing needs. Compare a damage-only gear choice against the healing and survival it costs your party.
classes.variant: For more group utility, replace an optional damage stigma with the needed support choice. Count the equipped four slots after every swap.
classes.lab: The Lab’s Cleric damage logic uses observed target/debuff windows; it does not read dependable party-health state. It therefore cannot decide when your group needs a heal or guarantee a reset chain.
classes.pitfall: Protection toggles can be switched off by a repeated macro press. Keep them outside the loop.

classes.name: Chanter
classes.intro: React to Dark Crush opportunities while sustaining melee pressure. Keep mantras, healing and crowd-control responses outside the repeating loop.
core: Damage core and its activation opportunities.
opener: Enable the chosen mantras once.
Create a valid Dark Crush opportunity with an available trigger.
Take Dark Crush promptly; resume the sustained lines.
Use Wave Blow when Stun is available, and stop for group recovery or mechanics.
progression: Do not assume Dark Crush has no cooldown until its actual specialty is selected.
Keep openers manual while learning their trigger windows.
Treat the Onslaught weave as a sustained pattern, not proof of a mandatory chain.
classes.gear: Invest in the damage core and support uptime. Useful combat speed and cooldown reduction compete with recovery and survival needs; evaluate the whole encounter.
classes.variant: A control-focused PvP preset needs different stigmas and timing. This baseline keeps group utilities manual rather than folding them into a damage-only macro.
classes.lab: Current Lab evidence gives Dark Crush a 2s opportunity after Impactful Crush or Spinning Strike, with a 5s base cooldown. Wave Blow reacts to observed Stun and applies Knockdown; it is not queued after Knockdown already exists.
classes.pitfall: A mantra in a repeating macro can toggle itself off. A visible stagger break is an opportunity to check state, not permission to assume every control skill is valid.
